mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, proxied by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and thus a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Significant negative 20-day forward returns when HOUST shows persistent upward momentum but SPX declines, or earnings revisions turn negative.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment, measured by PAYEMS, reduces labor market uncertainty and boosts investor confidence, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Negative 60-day forward returns when PAYEMS shows strong upward trends but SPX underperforms, or persistent negative earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2%, the S&P 500 anticipates a Fed rate hike, producing a negative 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns turn positive when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2% but no rate hike follows, or inflation decelerates without SPX decline.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand, which raises the probability of earnings disappointments and drives a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Positive 5-day returns when INDPRO shows consistent declines but SPX rises, or supply-chain improvements coincide without earnings recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising home sales (implied by HOUST) generate optimism about consumer wealth and corporate profits, producing a positive 20-day forward return even without fundamental earnings changes.
candidate_trigger: HOUST trend up for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant forward return when HOUST trends up but SPX remains flat, or negative earnings revisions offset the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in job openings (PAYEMS) during a low unemployment regime is interpreted as a labor market tightening that raises risk premiums and depresses equity valuations, causing a negative 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: Positive 60-day returns when PAYEMS spikes but unemployment falls and SPX outperforms, or risk sentiment improves without labor data.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 expects persistent higher borrowing costs, producing a negative 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: Positive returns when FEDFUNDS stays high but rates cut later, or SPX rises on other factors without rate sensitivity.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with a drop in consumer confidence (implied by HOUST) creates dual supply-demand pressures that drive a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Positive 5-day returns when both INDPRO and HOUST decline but SPX rises, or macro events explain SPX gains without supply weakness.
